description.p: GT-STACER is a modernised fork of Stacer by Oguzhan INAN, rebuilt with Qt 6 and C++ 17 for 2026. It provides a single unified interface for monitoring system resources, managing services and startup items, cleaning caches, and inspecting installed packages across 28+ package managers.

GT-STACER هو انشقاق محدّث من Stacer بقلم Oguzhan INAN، أُعيد بناؤه بـ Qt 6 و C++ 17 لعام 2026. يوفّر واجهة موحّدة لمراقبة موارد النظام، وإدارة الخدمات وبرامج بدء التشغيل، وتنظيف الذواكر المؤقتة، وإدارة الحزم المثبّتة عبر أكثر من 28 مدير حزم.

ul.li: Real-time CPU / memory / disk / network / GPU / temperature / battery dashboards
System cleaner with per-application drill-down for cache directories
Service manager (systemd / OpenRC / runit / s6 / SysV)
Startup application editor with icons and toggle switches
Package uninstaller covering 13+ package managers (APT, DNF, Pacman, Zypper, Flatpak, Snap, …)
Configurable desktop notifications for CPU temperature, memory, disk and battery thresholds
19 translated languages, full RTL support for Arabic

description.p: Small point release following testing of 26.11.1:

ul.li: The "What's new" dialog now lists the correct release (26.11 highlights plus the 26.11.1 fixes) instead of stale 26.10 content
The update check now compares versions across any number of components, so stable updates are recognised whatever the numbering and sequence

description.p: Bug-fix point release on top of 26.11:

ul.li: Firewall page no longer reports "no supported firewall" when ufw/firewalld is installed — the app now keeps the sbin directories on PATH so admin tools are detected
The in-app update check now understands patch versions (YY.MM.PATCH), so point releases are offered correctly
The Uninstaller becomes a full Package & Software Manager: install, upgrade and remove software from your system package manager, Flatpak and Snap, in a tabbed page

Manage opendesktop.org / KNewStuff store add-ons (themes, icons, plasmoids…) and integrate AppImages into your app menu — GearLever-compatible, reading its folder and settings, extracting metadata without executing the AppImage
In-app updates: GT-STACER checks for a newer version and can download, verify (SHA-256) and install it (AppImage self-replace, or the package via pkexec)
Security: fixed a command-injection vulnerability in package search; all new package operations use no-shell argv with validated names
Processes default to busiest-first (CPU %); the tray tooltip shows temperature; table columns are freely resizable everywhere

System Relief is now disk-aware: it shows I/O pressure (PSI) and per-process disk usage, can lower a busy process's I/O priority (ionice) instead of freezing it, and offers a one-click switch to the BFQ scheduler for a responsive old HDD under load
The Power timer (scheduled shutdown / restart / suspend / hibernate) is now available on the Power page as well as in Settings
A re-openable welcome tour and a "what's new" dialog shown after each update — both translated and with an in-dialog language picker
Optional update check that notifies when a newer release is out, and a "copy share text" button
Services moved under Processes in the sidebar; the Arabic language label simplified

description.p: Backup, snapshots and file recovery — a data-safety release. Highlights:

ul.li: Backup (new): system restore points via Timeshift, Snapper or ZFS, with the ideal engine for your filesystem auto-selected (and a choice when more than one is available), plus an rsync mirror of your home directory to another disk with live progress
Recovery (new): a graphical front-end for PhotoRec that carves lost or deleted files from a disk, partition or image — pick specific file types and have each type sorted into its own folder
System Cleaner can create a restore point before irreversible root-level cleanups (e.g. removing old kernels)
Sidebar reorganized by workflow; status pills on Firewall and Backup; assorted layout and translation fixes (Settings now scrolls on small windows)

description.p: Network & power tools, plus cross-desktop power integration. Highlights:

ul.li: Connections (new): live TCP/UDP sockets from ss with their owning process, a filter, and auto-refresh
Power (new): switch the power profile (power-profiles-daemon, or cpufreq governors), a laptop battery charge-limit, and a cross-desktop "keep awake" that blocks automatic sleep and screen locking
Firewall (new): enable/disable ufw or firewalld and add or remove port rules, with a single authorization per action
Keep-awake integrates with the desktop's own power UI over D-Bus and detects a block set elsewhere (e.g. KDE); a tray badge and a desktop notification signal the state
Refresh timers now pause when a page is not shown; per-page settings persisted
Startup Apps: autostart entries now launch (freedesktop-compliant writer), plus Flatpak/Snap detection and a per-entry start delay
Settings: start on login toggle, and a Power timer (shut down / restart / suspend / hibernate after N minutes)
System Relief (new): temporarily freeze idle, non-critical apps to relieve RAM/CPU pressure, then thaw them — manual or automatic
Uninstaller: full-page progress overlay during removal
Arabic UI back to 100 %; GPU renamed to "بطاقة الرسوميات"
Multi-field process search (PID, name, cmdline, user)
Six process actions with critical-process safety guard
Multi-package uninstall with sequential progress
Flatpak / Snap drill-down in System Cleaner
Dynamic package-cache labelling (APT / DNF / Pacman / Zypper / …)
Configurable notification thresholds
19 translation files compiled (Arabic 100 %, French 83 %)
